title: Bounds on the closed-rich constant of infinite words
summary: A finite word $w$ is called \textit{closed} if it has length at most 1 or it contains a proper factor that occurs both as a prefix and as a suffix but does not have internal occurrences in $w$. An infinite word $u$ is called \textit{closed-rich} if the infimum of all possible ratios between the number of closed factors within any factor $w$ of $u$ and square of the length of $w$ exists and is positive.
